content:
Sasquatch Resources Corp. (CSE: SASQ) has successfully closed the acquisition of the Echo Property, a gold exploration site consisting of eight mineral claims situated about 10km from Cowichan Lake on Vancouver Island, British Columbia. The transaction involved issuing 1,250,000 common shares at $0.105 each, totaling $131,250, along with granting a 2% net smelter return royalty on the property. Recent channel sampling over a 19-metre surface exposure yielded an average grade of 49.61 g/t gold, attracting investor attention as the company plans its next exploration steps at the location.

Key Points

  • Sasquatch Resources Corp. (CSE: SASQ) has completed the Echo Property acquisition on Vancouver Island, British Columbia.
  • The purchase price of $131,250 was paid through 1,250,000 common shares at $0.105 each, plus a 2% NSR royalty; shares are subject to a four-month hold expiring March 17, 2027.
  • Five continuous 3.8-metre channel samples across a 19-metre zone averaged 49.61 g/t gold, with individual assays ranging from 15.05 g/t to 100.0 g/t gold.
  • The company issued 2,375,000 stock options at $0.135 per share, exercisable for ten years and vesting immediately.

Echo Property Channel Sampling Reveals High-Grade Gold at Surface

Vice President of Exploration Justin Deveault conducted a 19-metre continuous channel sample across the Echo Showing in five consecutive 3.8-metre segments. ALS Canada Ltd. analyzed the samples using the Au-AA25 Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy method, reporting gold grades of 15.05, 23.8, 100.0, 32.9, and 51.3 g/t respectively, averaging 49.61 g/t gold over the entire 19 metres. The true width of the mineralization remains undetermined. Originally discovered in 1957, the showing is accessible via a logging road just minutes from paved routes in the Cowichan Valley.

Historical Exploration and Drilling Limitations at Echo Showing

Historical information from the Minfile database, not independently verified by Sasquatch, includes surface sampling results of approximately 95 g/t gold over 4.6 metres and bulk samples averaging about 54 g/t gold. Four diamond drill holes by Consolidated Ramrod Gold Corp. in 1993 targeted areas away from the main showing and returned poor results. Sasquatch’s review suggests these drill holes may not have effectively tested the mineralized zone, leaving the full extent of mineralization unknown. One historical drill hole initiated within the showing encountered gold in cuttings but suffered from poor core recovery.

Related-Party Acquisition and Stock Option Issuance

The Echo Property was acquired from Justin Deveault, Andrew Clarke, and Rory Munroe under an asset purchase agreement dated November 5, 2026. As Deveault is a Sasquatch director, this constitutes a related-party transaction under Multilateral Instrument 61-101, but the company qualifies for exemptions from formal valuation and minority shareholder approval. Additionally, Sasquatch granted 2,375,000 stock options to directors, officers, and consultants, exercisable at $0.135 per share for ten years and vesting immediately, also structured under MI 61-101 exemptions.

Echo Property Enhances Sasquatch’s Vancouver Island Exploration Portfolio

This acquisition adds to Sasquatch’s existing portfolio, which includes the Mount Sicker, Blue Grouse, Santana, Alberni, and Slesse properties. The company emphasizes a low-capital, low-environmental-impact strategy focused on reclaiming mineralized waste rock at legacy mine sites and logging roads. The technical data in this release was reviewed and approved by independent Qualified Person Darcy Vis, B.Sc., P.Geo., in accordance with National Instrument 43-101. The immediate effect on Sasquatch’s share price was not evident from publicly available information.
